items.detail: The **S&P 500 fell 1.2%** to close at **7,408.30** on Thursday, while the Nasdaq sank **2.2% to 25,137.69** — a second brutal session led by megacap tech.
items.why: Big Tech Q2 earnings reignited AI capital-spending fears just as Brent crude broke $100 on Middle East supply threats, driving a broad risk-off move.

items.detail: **Alphabet slid ~5%** after lifting its 2026 capex guidance to as much as **$205 billion**, and Tesla's Elon Musk flagged a "massive capex year" — the Magnificent Seven shed roughly **$797 billion** in a single session, their worst drop since April 2025.
items.why: Investors read the record spending as proof that AI demand, while strong, is becoming far more expensive to deliver and is squeezing free cash flow.

items.detail: **Brent crude topped $100/bbl** for the first time in the cycle, adding an inflation shock on top of the tech selloff and lifting the US 10-year Treasury yield toward **4.7%**.
items.why: Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and President Trump threatened to strike Iranian infrastructure, spiking geopolitical risk premium.

items.detail: Friday's session stabilized: the **S&P 500 edged up 0.05% to 7,411.98** and the Dow rose ~0.5%, though the Nasdaq slipped another 0.6% and **Sandisk tumbled 11%**.
items.why: Oil retreated modestly and real estate and financials led a rotation out of technology, letting the broad index steady even as chip and megacap names kept falling.

items.detail: The **Nifty 50 fell 0.43% to 23,767.45** and the Sensex dropped 331.62 points to **76,059.77**, closing below 23,800 for a **fifth straight losing session**.
items.why: Brent crude crossing $100 on Red Sea attacks revived fears over India's import bill, trade deficit, rupee and corporate margins, keeping investors defensive.

items.detail: **Auto was the biggest laggard**, followed by energy, metals and realty, while the **Nifty IT index bucked the trend, rising ~0.8%**.
items.why: Costlier crude threatens fuel-sensitive autos and margins for energy and metals, whereas dollar-earning IT names benefit from a weaker rupee.

items.detail: The **rupee weakened toward ₹96.63/$** and foreign investors stayed net sellers, having offloaded roughly **₹3,000 crore** of equities in the prior session.
items.why: The US 10-year yield near 4.7% makes US debt more attractive versus emerging-market equities, pressuring the rupee and fueling continued FII outflows.

items.detail: **Bitcoin fell ~1.6%**, sliding from an open near **$65,048 to about $64,305**, as digital assets tracked the broader risk-off move.
items.why: Higher oil prices and new tariff measures lifted US inflation expectations and Treasury yields, luring institutional money away from risk assets like crypto.

items.detail: US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted **$225.2 million in net outflows**, snapping a seven-day inflow streak that had gathered roughly **$999 million**.
items.why: The global risk-asset selloff and rising yields prompted institutions to pull back from the ETFs despite the recent legislative momentum on crypto.

items.detail: **Ethereum dropped ~2.9% to about $1,861** and **Solana slid ~2.8% to $73.97**, the biggest loser among the top-10 coins, with XRP down ~2.5%.
items.why: Higher-beta altcoins amplified Bitcoin's decline as leverage flushed out — roughly $280 million in positions were liquidated across the market.

items.detail: The **CLARITY Act remains stalled** in the Senate at Calendar No. 423, with three disputes — ethics rules, DeFi developer shields and stablecoin yield — blocking the Democratic votes needed to clear the 60-vote threshold before the August recess.
About **$1.43 billion** of Bitcoin and Ethereum options expired on July 24, and Poolin Technology — once the largest Bitcoin mining pool — filed for **Chapter 11 bankruptcy**.

crossCuttingTheme: Brent crude above $100 on Red Sea tanker attacks and Iran conflict is the shared driver — it is lifting inflation expectations and US Treasury yields toward 4.7%, triggering a synchronized, inflation-led risk-off that is hitting US equities, Indian stocks and the rupee, and crypto all at once.
